Pronunciation note for this grammar point:
A non-defining clause is spoken as a separate tone unit: the report, / which we sent in June, / is late. The defining clause runs as one unit with no pause.
Read it aloud, then record yourself: the main stress falls on the content word, not on the hedge.

elements.content: Grammar focus: Defining and Non-Defining Relative Clauses.

Ask whether the reader already knows which thing you mean. If not, the clause identifies it: no commas, that is fine, and the pronoun can vanish when it is the object. If yes, the clause only adds: commas, no that, and the pronoun must stay.

defining, no commas — identifies the noun: the report that we sent
non-defining, commas — adds information: the report, which we sent in June,
that — defining only: the team that won the bid
who / which — both types, people and things: my manager, who joined in May,
pronoun omitted — defining, object: the report we sent
whose — possession, both types: the analyst whose model failed
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Complete: 'The engineer ___ designed the bridge has retired.'
2. Which sentence is correct?
options: The plan, that we approved, failed.
The plan, which we approved, failed.

elements.content: 3. Complete: 'The file ___ we sent was corrupted.'
Read and listen: three examples in context.

The report that we sent is late. — Defining: tells you which report. (No commas, that is allowed.)
The report, which we sent in June, is late. — Non-defining: extra information. (Commas, never that.)
The team that won the bid has disbanded. — Defining: identifies the team. (Removing it changes the meaning.)
What do you observe?

A defining relative clause identifies which person or thing is meant, so it carries no commas and that is allowed. A non-defining clause adds information about something already identified, so it sits between commas, that is not allowed, and who or which is required. In a defining clause the pronoun can be left out when it is the object: the report we sent. It cannot be left out in a non-defining clause.
1. Which clause can use that?
2. Does removing a non-defining clause change which thing you mean?
options: No: the thing is already identified.

elements.content: State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: I can discuss ethical issues in entertainment.

Success criteria:
- I can use that only in a defining clause.
- I can punctuate a non-defining clause with commas.
- I can drop the object pronoun in a defining clause.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ My manager, that joined in May, approved it (that in a non-defining clause) → ✅ My manager, who joined in May, approved it
❌ The report which we sent in June is late and out of date (missing commas around a non-defining clause) → ✅ The report, which we sent in June, is late and out of date
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

The figures we published in March were revised.
The figures, which we published in March, were revised.
The client whose contract lapsed has reappeared.
